claims.text: CT or MRI of the head.
claims.quote: Testing usually includes CT or MRI of the head

claims.text: Infection: CBC, blood cultures, chest x-ray, urinalysis.
claims.quote: Tests for suspected infection (eg, complete blood count [CBC], blood cultures, chest radiography, urinalysis)
Evaluation for hypoxia (pulse oximetry or arterial blood gases)

claims.text: Electrolytes, BUN, creatinine, glucose, and levels of any drug suspected of toxicity.
claims.quote: Measurement of electrolytes, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine, plasma glucose, and blood levels of any medications suspected to have toxic effects

claims.text: If still unclear: liver tests, calcium and albumin, TSH, vitamin B12, ESR and/or CRP, ANA, and RPR or VDRL.
claims.quote: If the diagnosis is unclear, further testing may include liver tests, measurement of serum calcium and albumin , thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), vitamin B12, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and/or C-reactive protein (CRP), antinuclear antibody (ANA), and a test for syphilis (eg, rapid plasma reagin [RPR] or Venereal Disease Research Laboratory [VDRL] test).

claims.text: Next: CSF analysis (meningitis, encephalitis, subarachnoid hemorrhage), serum ammonia, heavy metals.
claims.quote: If the diagnosis is still unclear, testing may include cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis (particularly to exclude meningitis, encephalitis, or subarachnoid hemorrhage), measurement of serum ammonia, and testing to check for heavy metals.

claims.text: EEG when nonconvulsive seizures or status epilepticus are suspected (subtle twitches, automatisms, fluctuating confusion and drowsiness).
claims.quote: If nonconvulsive seizure activity, including status epilepticus, is suspected (suggested by subtle motor twitches, automatisms, and a fluctuating pattern of bewilderment and drowsiness), electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring should be done.
